description: A single-panel scatter-plus-fit plot used to evaluate the material constant C of the hot-deformation constitutive relation. The horizontal axis is labelled ln(ε/ε_p)+1−ε/ε_p and runs from −3 to 0 in unit tick steps; the vertical axis is labelled ln(σ/σ_p) and runs from −0.45 to 0.00 with ticks at −0.45, −0.30, −0.15 and 0.00. A legend in the upper-left identifies the '+' symbols as "Discrete data points" and the red line as "Linear fit of data points". Roughly twenty '+' points rise from the lower-left corner region (between the −0.45 and −0.30 gridlines, at x between −3 and −2) up to the origin at (0, 0), scattering tightly around the red straight line, which is drawn over essentially the same range. Printed inside the lower-right of the frame is the fit result "C = 0.1461, R = 0.9728", so the fitted slope yields C and the fit quality is reported as R. The figure demonstrates that ln(σ/σ_p) is linearly proportional to ln(ε/ε_p)+1−ε/ε_p under the stated test condition, which justifies extracting C from a straight-line fit; the condition is 1050 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹ per the caption.

subfigures.description: Single scatter plot of ln(σ/σ_p) versus ln(ε/ε_p)+1−ε/ε_p with about twenty '+' discrete data points and a red linear fit line through them; legend reads 'Discrete data points' and 'Linear fit of data points', and the annotation 'C = 0.1461, R = 0.9728' is printed in the lower right.

observations.observation: The horizontal axis is labelled ln(ε/ε_p)+1−ε/ε_p and spans −3 to 0 with unit ticks.
The vertical axis is labelled ln(σ/σ_p) and spans −0.45 to 0.00 with ticks at −0.45, −0.30, −0.15 and 0.00.
The legend contains two entries: '+' = 'Discrete data points' and red line = 'Linear fit of data points'.
The fitted result printed inside the plot frame is 'C = 0.1461, R = 0.9728'.
About twenty '+' discrete data points lie close to the red straight line, with only small scatter; individual point coordinates are not labelled.
The red linear fit line is drawn from roughly the lower-left corner of the data range up to the origin region (x ≈ 0), covering approximately the same x-interval as the data points.
The leftmost data point sits between the −0.30 and −0.45 horizontal gridlines, at an x position between −3 and −2.
The data points appear to lie slightly above the fitted line in the middle of the range and converge with it near both ends; no numeric deviation is printed.
The figure is stated to correspond to the condition of 1050 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹.
C is obtained from the slope fitted to ln(σ/σ_p) versus [ln(ε/ε_p)+1−ε/ε_p], and the fitting result at 1050 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹ is shown in this figure.
Using the same fitting method, the material constant C can also be obtained at other temperatures and strain rates.
